endorsements.quote: The validation set must be fully independent from the development data in temporal (different acquisition periods), geographic (different institutions), or both 30 , 31 .
Crucially, prior to any data access or analysis, a formal study protocol and a detailed statistical analysis plan (SAP) must be explicitly prespecified.

Beyond discrimination, probabilistic models must report calibration metrics (e.g., Brier score, expected calibration error [ECE], and reliability plots) together with validated uncertainty estimates to evaluate prediction reliability, particularly for heterogeneous data, edge cases, and out-of-distribution inputs.
Reference standard construction should maintain strict separation between the algorithm team and the annotation team.

The model runs in real time in the background without displaying outputs to clinicians, allowing comprehensive assessment of its behavior under authentic data flow conditions, including data preprocessing, inference latency, failure rates, and engineering bottlenecks 46 – 48 .

This phase typically employs a multidimensional framework based on prospective randomized controlled trials (Method 6), which use controlled comparisons to eliminate confounding and ensure that any observed benefit can be causally attributed to AI 110 , 111 .

When prespecified alerting thresholds are breached, such as ≥5% AUROC decline, ≥10% sensitivity loss, subgroup-specific degradation, fairness-drift thresholds, or safety-critical error triggers, a structured de-implementation pathway must be automatically activated.

Operationalizing post-market surveillance requires a risk-stratified monitoring cadence, with high-risk diagnostic systems undergoing daily or weekly automated checks and lower-risk applications monitored on a monthly basis.
Statistical process-control methods (e.g., CUSUM, EWMA, and Shewhart control charts) should be deployed to dynamically detect gradual or abrupt drift in real-world data streams.

Key subgroup analyzes, stratified by pathological severity, data‑source heterogeneity, acquisition processes, and demographics, alongside formal AI-by-site interaction testing, are essential to avoid masking failure modes that may be hidden by “average performance” 40 , 42 .
Crucially, prior to initiating shadow-mode deployment, a formal monitoring protocol or a versioned analysis charter must be explicitly prespecified.
Any updated version must be treated as a new model and re‑evaluated on a new, independent third‑party dataset to preserve the integrity and independence of the evaluation process.

Regardless of the specific approach, the phase must ensure that AI versions, thresholds, and interfaces remain stable and traceable throughout the study; that failure modes and anomalous events arising in real workflows are systematically documented; that performance consistency is monitored across institutions, devices, and patient groups; and that comprehensive records of data governance, privacy protection, and model‑update processes are maintained.

To ensure methodological transparency, external validation studies in this phase must align with task-specific international standards: studies evaluating the standalone diagnostic accuracy of an AI tool should adhere to the STARD-AI statement 18 , whereas those validating multivariable individual risk prediction models should strictly follow the TRIPOD + AI guidelines 17 .

This pathway includes clear fall-back protocols, such as automatic rollback to a prior validated version, reverting the model to background shadow-mode tracking, temporary suspension of deployment, or full withdrawal, thereby safeguarding patient care while root-cause analysis and model retraining occur.

unlisted_practices: Lock model version, parameters, and decision thresholds before evaluation and permit no post-hoc tuning; treat any modification as a new model requiring re-evaluation.
Track cumulative compute costs and operational carbon footprint of AI maintenance and retraining during longitudinal post-market monitoring.
Include multiple centers (typically at least three) in external validation and perform formal AI-by-site interaction testing.
Use consecutive enrollment or random sampling in validation cohorts to preserve low-quality and complex cases and avoid spectrum bias.
Report prospective trials using SPIRIT-AI for protocol design and CONSORT-AI for reporting outcomes.
Incorporate decision-curve analysis to estimate net clinical benefit in evaluation of probabilistic and decision-support AI.
Standardize or systematically vary interface elements such as alert saliency and confidence display in human-AI studies to separate UI-driven coercion from automation bias.
Include a familiarization phase and case reshuffling in reader studies to control learning and order effects.

screen.reason: This is a framework paper proposing a five-phase lifecycle evaluation and governance framework for medical AI systems.
